text: The Moon's surface gravity is 1.62 metres per second squared, about one sixth of Earth's
as_written: one point six two metres per second squared, about one sixth of ours
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

text: Earth's atmosphere is about 78% nitrogen, 21% oxygen and a little under 1% argon
as_written: about seventy eight percent nitrogen, twenty one percent oxygen, and a little under one percent argon
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet (NSSDCA)

text: The Moon is about 3,500 km across (diameter about 3,475 km)
as_written: about three and a half thousand kilometres across
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

text: Standard sea-level pressure is about 101,325 pascals
as_written: about one hundred and one thousand pascals
source: International Standard Atmosphere (ICAO / ISO 2533)

text: Giving the Moon sea-level pressure requires about 2.4e18 kg of gas, from p = M g / (4 pi R^2) using lunar gravity and radius
as_written: roughly two point four quintillion kilograms of gas
source: Derived calculation using NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet values for gravity and radius

text: Earth's atmosphere has a mass of about 5.1e18 kg
as_written: about five point one quintillion kilograms
source: Trenberth and Smith 2005, Journal of Climate, The Mass of the Atmosphere

text: The Moon's surface area is about one thirteenth of Earth's
as_written: about one thirteenth of the surface area of Earth
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon and Earth Fact Sheets (radius 1,737 km vs 6,371 km, area ratio about 0.074)

text: Earth's atmospheric scale height is about 8.5 km
as_written: a characteristic height of about eight and a half kilometres
source: NASA Earth Fact Sheet (scale height 8.5 km)

text: With one sixth of the gravity, the same air would have a scale height about six times larger, near 50 km (H = kT/mg)
as_written: a characteristic height near fifty kilometres
source: Derived from hydrostatic equilibrium, scale height H = kT/(mg), with Moon fact sheet gravity

text: Column mass of air above a square metre is p/g, so six times larger on the Moon at equal pressure
as_written: about six times as many air molecules
source: Derived from hydrostatic balance, using NASA Moon Fact Sheet gravity

text: The lunar atmosphere is more than a hundred trillion times thinner than Earth's sea-level air, as measured by the Apollo 17 Lunar Atmospheric Composition Experiment
as_written: more than a hundred trillion times thinner than the air you are breathing
source: Apollo 17 LACE (Hoffman et al., 1973); NASA LADEE mission results

text: Apollo suits operated at about 3.7 psi of pure oxygen
as_written: about three point seven pounds per square inch of pure oxygen
source: NASA Apollo Experience Report, Apollo space suit assembly

text: Sea-level atmospheric pressure is about 14.7 psi
as_written: fourteen point seven
source: International Standard Atmosphere

text: Outside pressure of 14.7 psi would be about four times the suit's 3.7 psi
as_written: about four times harder
source: Derived from 14.7 / 3.7 using NASA Apollo suit figures

text: Standard sea-level air temperature is 15 degrees Celsius
as_written: at a pleasant fifteen degrees
source: International Standard Atmosphere

text: Sound travels at about 340 m/s in 15 degree air
as_written: about three hundred and forty metres per second
source: International Standard Atmosphere (speed of sound 340.3 m/s)

text: Astronauts described the smell of lunar dust as like spent gunpowder
as_written: spent gunpowder
source: Apollo 11, 12 and 17 crew post-mission debriefs and NASA accounts (e.g. NASA, Dirty Dust Issue)

text: The Moon turns once in a little over 29 days relative to the Sun (synodic period 29.53 days), so the Sun moves about half a degree per hour
as_written: about half a degree per hour
source: Derived from lunar synodic period 29.53 days, NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

text: A lunar day is about 29.5 Earth days
as_written: about twenty nine and a half Earth days long
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet (synodic period 29.53 days)

text: Earth is about 3.7 times wider in the lunar sky than the Moon appears from Earth (diameters 12,742 km vs 3,475 km at similar distance)
as_written: almost four times wider than the Moon looks from here
source: NASA NSSDCA Earth and Moon Fact Sheets

text: Apollo 15 astronaut David Scott dropped a hammer and a falcon feather on the Moon in 1971 and they landed together
as_written: In nineteen seventy one, on Apollo fifteen, David Scott
source: NASA Apollo 15 Mission Report and surface film footage

text: Terminal speed scales with the square root of gravity, so a feather at one sixth gravity would settle at about 0.41 of its Earth speed
as_written: about two fifths of the speed it falls at on Earth
source: Derived from quadratic drag terminal velocity v = sqrt(2mg/(rho Cd A))

text: Equatorial lunar noon temperature reaches about 127 degrees Celsius
as_written: about one hundred and twenty seven degrees Celsius
source: NASA Moon facts; LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer

text: Threshold wind speed for lifting grains scales with the square root of gravity
as_written: scales with the square root of gravity
source: Bagnold 1941, The Physics of Blown Sand and Desert Dunes; Shao and Lu 2000, J. Geophysical Research

text: Apollo 17 astronaut Harrison Schmitt reported lunar hay fever from dust
as_written: Harrison Schmitt, on Apollo seventeen, developed what he called lunar hay fever
source: NASA Apollo 17 Technical Crew Debriefing; NASA Science, The Moon Dust Problem

text: Estimates of cosmic dust entering Earth's atmosphere range from about 5 to 300 tonnes per day
as_written: range from about five to three hundred tonnes
source: Plane 2012, Chemical Society Reviews, Cosmic dust in the earth's atmosphere

text: The Chelyabinsk meteor of 2013 was about 20 metres wide and broke windows across the city
as_written: about twenty metres wide
source: NASA/JPL Near Earth Object Program; Popova et al. 2013, Science

text: The Moon's surface falls to about minus 173 degrees Celsius at night
as_written: about minus one hundred and seventy three degrees Celsius
source: NASA Moon facts; LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer

text: The noon to midnight temperature swing is about 300 degrees (127 to minus 173)
as_written: the difference of three hundred degrees between noon and midnight
source: NASA Moon facts; LRO Diviner Lunar Radiometer

text: Venus rotates once in about 243 Earth days
as_written: turns once every two hundred and forty three Earth days
source: NASA NSSDCA Venus Fact Sheet

text: Venus surface temperature is about 465 degrees Celsius (737 K)
as_written: about four hundred and sixty five degrees Celsius
source: NASA NSSDCA Venus Fact Sheet

text: Venus surface pressure is about 92 bar, about 92 times Earth's
as_written: about ninety two times the surface pressure of Earth
source: NASA NSSDCA Venus Fact Sheet

text: A 1997 study found thin atmospheres can transport enough heat to the night side of tidally locked planets to prevent atmospheric collapse
as_written: a well known study in nineteen ninety seven
source: Joshi, Haberle and Reynolds 1997, Icarus, Simulations of the atmospheres of synchronously rotating terrestrial planets orbiting M dwarfs

text: The Moon's Bond albedo is about 0.11, reflecting about eleven percent of sunlight
as_written: only about eleven percent of the sunlight
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

text: The Moon's black-body temperature is about 270.7 K
as_written: about two hundred and seventy kelvin
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon Fact Sheet

text: Lunar escape velocity is 2.38 km/s and Earth's is 11.2 km/s
as_written: two point three eight kilometres per second
source: NASA NSSDCA Moon and Earth Fact Sheets

text: Earth's escape velocity is 11.2 km/s
as_written: eleven point two
source: NASA NSSDCA Earth Fact Sheet

text: Mars's escape velocity is about 5.03 km/s, more than twice the Moon's
as_written: about five kilometres per second, more than twice the Moon's
source: NASA NSSDCA Mars Fact Sheet

text: MAVEN found solar wind stripping removed a large share of Mars's atmosphere
as_written: stripped away a large share of the Martian atmosphere
source: NASA MAVEN mission; Jakosky et al. 2015 and 2018, Science

text: The Moon passes through Earth's magnetotail for about six days each month around full Moon
as_written: for about six days around full Moon
source: NASA ARTEMIS mission; NASA Science, The Moon and Earth's magnetotail

text: Volcanic outgassing about 3.5 billion years ago may have given the Moon a transient atmosphere lasting about 70 million years
as_written: about seventy million years
source: Needham and Kring 2017, Earth and Planetary Science Letters, Lunar volcanism produced a transient atmosphere around the ancient Moon

text: The Moon is about 4.5 billion years old
as_written: about four and a half billion years old
source: NASA Science, Moon formation; Barboni et al. 2017, Science Advances

text: Titan's escape velocity is about 2.64 km/s
as_written: about two point six four kilometres per second
source: NASA NSSDCA Saturn Satellite Fact Sheet

text: Titan's surface gravity (1.35 m/s2) is lower than the Moon's (1.62 m/s2)
as_written: a surface gravity lower than the Moon's
source: NASA NSSDCA Saturn Satellite Fact Sheet

text: Titan's surface pressure is about 1.5 bar, about one and a half times Earth's
as_written: about one and a half times as thick as ours at the surface
source: ESA Huygens probe results; NASA Titan fact sheet

text: Titan's surface temperature is about 94 K, about minus 179 degrees Celsius
as_written: about minus one hundred and seventy nine degrees Celsius
source: ESA Huygens probe results; NASA Titan fact sheet

text: Air density at sea level and 15 degrees is about 1.2 kg per cubic metre
as_written: about one point two kilograms per cubic metre
source: International Standard Atmosphere (1.225 kg/m3)

text: Induced power for flight scales with weight to the power 3/2, so one sixth weight needs about 6^1.5, roughly 15 times less power
as_written: about fifteen times less power
source: Derived from lifting-line / actuator disc theory, e.g. Anderson, Fundamentals of Aerodynamics

text: Six to the power of one and a half is about fifteen
as_written: Six raised to the power of one and a half is about fifteen
source: Arithmetic (6^1.5 = 14.7)

text: The Gossamer Albatross, pedalled by Bryan Allen, crossed the English Channel in 1979, covering 35.8 km in 2 hours 49 minutes
as_written: thirty five point eight kilometres in two hours and forty nine minutes
source: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum, Gossamer Albatross; MacCready et al.

text: Lunar jumps carry about six times higher than on Earth because gravity is a sixth
as_written: which already carries you six times higher than on Earth
source: Derived from ballistic motion h = v^2/2g with NASA Moon Fact Sheet gravity
